description: Route-inventory annotations (plan §1.2/§1.5): recorded evidence for every dynamic (non-literal) executeCommand dispatch site, every internal reference to a command VS Code auto-registers rather than the extension, and every route whose mechanical surface drifted from the immutable pre-gate snapshot (workflow-route-pregate-v1.json). Verified by scripts/verifyWorkflowRoutes.mjs: an unannotated dynamic dispatch or pre-gate drift fails closed, a stale sourceSpan or stability digest fails, and an annotation matching no live site/drift fails. Annotations cannot replace an early gate (edgeKind "gateReplacement" is rejected).

annotations.planSection: §1.2 route table (Current stage: every branch and caller)
annotations.rationale: The composite current-stage dispatcher resolves the stage's action command from its static per-stage table and forwards via executeCommand. Every resolvable value is one of the registered per-stage AI commands, each of which carries its own first-statement legacy AI gate; the dispatcher itself is additionally gated by applyCurrentStage.v1 before this line can run.

The automation chain's default dependency executes the follow-up command chosen from its static chain definition (stage follow-up commands only). Each target is a registered command whose own gate/barrier discipline applies at the callee; no computed/user-supplied command id can enter the chain.

The global assistant's action table binds each assistant action to a fixed registered command (see the treeBindings recorded on the corresponding route rows: markTaskDone, nextStage, runReviewWithAI, fastForwardReviewWithAI, pauseTask, resumeTask, archive/unarchive, pin/unpin). The dispatch expression reads only from that static table; gates apply at each callee.

Template over the class's constant viewType — resolves to the single constant string "vs-code-ai-helper.chatView.focus", the focus command VS Code auto-registers for the contributed chat view. Pure UI focus; no workflow route.

tryRun executes a command id taken from the settings webview's own static command wiring (model-configuration commands registered in configureStepModels.ts). Pure settings UI; no AI/workflow route is reachable through it.

The webview-deps executeCommand adapter passed into the settings view's message handling — a thin promise wrapper around vscode.commands.executeCommand used only by the static settings-command wiring above it.
Runs the usage-hint command declared in the settings view's static usage table (settings/model configuration commands only).
Fallback variant of the usage-hint dispatch above; same static table, same settings-only reachability.

runAction re-dispatches a notification row's stored follow-up command. Action descriptors are created only by production code posting notifications (e.g. "Publish Anyway" → commitAndPushTask) with literal command ids that appear as treeBindings on their route rows; each callee's own gate/guard applies at dispatch time.

The status-bar quick-pick menu dispatches the selected item's command from its static menu definition (resumeTask, viewTask, startNewTask — recorded as treeBindings on those rows); gates/guards apply at each callee.

"<viewId>.focus" commands are auto-registered by VS Code for every contributed view; the extension registers its own settingsView.focus (missing-model guard) but relies on the host-provided statusView.focus here. Not a workflow route.

annotations.planSection: §1.3 (fail-closed AI gates) / §8 Safety cohort / §7.8 edit-branch routing
annotations.rationale: The Safety cohort (plan §1.3) installed the first-statement legacy AI route gate for applyReview.v1 in this route's registering file. A subsequent Text-3/edit-routing fix (plan §1.3's 'gate before any read' requirement, review round addressing the Apply Review text/edit split) collapsed the wrapper's two sequential resolveTaskContext reads into one, and added an explicit assertLegacyAiRouteAllowedV0("applyReviewEdit.v1") check immediately after that single resolution — before the paused check, consent, or any further read — for an impl-high-review target, instead of relying solely on the downstream applyReviewWithAI delegate to gate it one function call later. A further round (AC-ROUTE-01 architectural blocker: 'genuinely separate static text/edit-root commands, not one dynamic command reading progress to branch') split the delegate target itself: the impl-high-review branch now issues its own literal executeCommand("vs-code-ai-helper.applyReviewEditWithAI", ...) call instead of forwarding to the shared applyReviewWithAI, so the edit route is reachable through a dedicated statically-registered command end to end. The mechanical change is fileGateRouteIds [applyReview.v1] -> [applyReview.v1, applyReviewEdit.v1] plus the new literal edge to applyReviewEditWithAI. Gate-before-read ordering is wiring-tested in legacyAiActionSafetyGateWiring.test.ts; the edit-gate-fires-in-the-wrapper behavior (and that the plan-review/text branch is unaffected) is covered by dedicated regression tests in commandArgNormalization.test.ts.

New dedicated edit-root command for Apply Review (AC-ROUTE-01 architectural blocker: 'genuinely separate static text/edit-root commands, not one dynamic command reading progress to branch'). Unlike the shared applyReviewWithAI, which must dynamically discover a {taskFolderPath}/no-arg dispatch's stage before it knows its branch, this command's mere existence proves edit intent: its handler asserts assertLegacyAiRouteAllowedV0("applyReviewEdit.v1") unconditionally as the literal first statement, before any argument normalization or read, then delegates to the same underlying applyReviewWithAI implementation (shared behavior is not the architectural problem the plan flags; one shared PUBLIC COMMAND identity for both branches was). At pregate-annotation time, applyReviewEdit.v1 was disabled pending plan §7/§7.8's edit migration, so this route always rejected, identically to the shared command's own edit branch. Status update (§7.8 edit-cohort cutover, this completion round): applyReviewEdit.v1 has since been removed from LEGACY_AI_ROUTE_DISABLED_V0 and is enabled — the delegate's edit branch now runs the sealed two-phase preflight/edit pipeline (runSealedImplementationV1) instead of the retired legacy runner. This annotation's own evidence (route addition since pregate, gate placement) is unaffected; only the disabled-at-the-time status note above is superseded. Evidence refresh 2026-08-03 (completion round, plan §8 Cleanup cohort): this row's fileGateRouteIds rollup lost "reviewSecondOpinion.v0", which is now removed outright from legacyAiActionSafetyGateV0.ts's registered route catalog (see that file's own evidence refresh) rather than merely staying disabled — no gate or registration logic at this row changed.

The §7.8 cutover made every edit-capable action (implementation.v1, fastForward.v1, applyReviewEdit.v1, lint.v1) run exclusively through the sealed two-phase pipeline, which only a Copilot-backed model can join — a CLI agent edits files with its own in-process tools that the extension never sees, so it cannot participate in the pipeline's request-local vscode.lm tool-calling loop at all. This silently required a Copilot subscription for implementation, with no CLI equivalent for the direct edit-mode path (runImplementationForModel/runImplementationWithCli) it replaced, even though that path remained fully implemented and tested — just orphaned (zero production callers; see runnerRegistry.ts's own evidence refresh). The new runImplementationOrSealedV1 is the actual entry point reviewActions.ts's executeImplementationRun and runLintingFixes.ts's AI fix pass now call (see their own evidence refreshes): it resolves the stage model's effective provider and calls runSealedImplementationV1 unchanged for a Copilot-resolved one, or this runImplementationForModel call directly for a CLI-resolved one — restoring the exact git-snapshot-based direct edit-mode invocation runImplementationWithAI used before the §7.8 cutover for all four edit-capable actions. This path has no preflight, receipts, or structured mid-run questions — CLI providers never had that and cannot participate in it — but is not a stub: same backup-model cascade, same quota/auth classification as the sealed path.

The Safety cohort (plan §1.3/§10.1) installed the non-throwing isLegacyAiRouteDisabledV0("commitPushMetadata.v1") query in commitAndPushTask.ts so the disabled AI metadata sub-step degrades to the deterministic fallback subject without breaking the non-AI commit flow; fileGateRouteIds [] -> [commitPushMetadata.v1] was the only mechanical change since the pre-gate snapshot. The Text-3 completion round (plan §10.2 point 4) further changed buildCommitMessage's return shape to a discriminated CommitMessageResultV1 so a "questions" outcome ends this Commit and Push attempt (no modal shown, no fallback-subject commit) instead of silently falling back, and threaded an optional seedCommitMessage argument through commitAndPushTaskCore/reviewCommitMessage so Resume's resumed metadata seeds a fresh attempt's review dialog directly. The early duplicate-invocation token (CommitPushEarlyGateV0) landed in an earlier cohort but does not alter this row's mechanical identity. Evidence refresh 2026-07-29 (closing an implementation-review completion blocker: metadata Resume generated content ahead of fresh Git validation/lint and only afterward offered a separate unlinked public-command notification): seedCommitMessage/extractSeedCommitMessage are removed entirely. resumeCommitPushMetadataInteractionV1 (commitAndPushTask.ts) now calls this SAME public commitAndPushTask entry point directly (with a private resumeInteraction request carrying the pending interaction ref, never set by UI surfaces) instead of calling coordinator.resumeAction itself — so an explicit Chat Resume of a commitPushMetadata.v1 question is now itself one more caller of this exact route: it acquires this row's own process-global token, runs this row's own fresh git-readiness/index checks and lint, and only then runs the metadata attempt inside reviewCommitMessage. This is a genuinely new caller of the route (raising its stability digest) but not a new route or a change to the route's own gate/guard/target. Correction reversed 2026-08-02 (impl-high-review round, replacing the 2026-08-02 "Target-key correction" note above, which the review rejected as unapproved plan-scope reduction): a real commitPush.v1 lifecycle row now exists (commitPushRowV1.ts, registered in productionTaskActionRuntimeV1.ts) and IS this route's target. The public commitAndPushTask entry still acquires the independent process-global token first (plan §10.1, unchanged), then resolves the task and invokes commitPush.v1 through invokeLifecycleRowV1 (a new lifecycleServices side channel on LifecycleExecutionContextV1 carries TaskInventory/CurrentTaskStore/ChatViewProvider/ExtensionContext, since the Git workflow's live dependencies cannot be expressed as JSON rawInput); the row's execute delegates to commitAndPushTaskCore UNCHANGED (every check, prompt, and git command is identical) so the registry now genuinely owns eligibility, presentation, and settlement logging (plan §3.8) without altering commit/push behavior. Correction 2026-08-02 (impl-high-review round, closing a completion-review finding that this annotation overclaimed operation-lease ownership): at that point commitPushRowV1.ts set requiresTaskOperationLease: false — commitAndPushTaskCore's own nested reviewCommitMessage step invokes commitPushMetadata.v1 (also requiresTaskOperationLease: true) for this SAME task binding, and workflowLeaseStoreV1 then allowed only one lease per task binding regardless of action key, so a per-task coordinator lease held for this row's whole (long, interactive) duration would have self-deadlocked that nested provider call into duplicateRejected. Superseding correction 2026-08-02 (same round, completion-blocker follow-up closing the review's Commit/Push lease-ownership gap): commitPushRowV1.ts now sets requiresTaskOperationLease: true, and the self-deadlock is resolved instead of avoided — workflowLeaseStoreV1 gained acquireChild, a nested-lease primitive granted only while the exact matching parent operation currently holds the binding's lease; commitAndPushTaskCore now takes a coordinatorOperationId parameter (threaded from commitPushRowV1.ts's own context.operationId through executeCommitPushV1) and passes it into the nested commitPushMetadata.v1 call as parentOperationId, so that call opens a CHILD lease on this same binding instead of a top-level one. The coordinator's per-task lease is therefore now genuinely held for this row's whole execution span, layered ON TOP OF (not instead of) the independent process-global token (plan §3.8: "Commit/Push retains its independent process-global token") and commitAndPushTaskCore's own per-task runTrackedOperation lock, both unchanged. commitAndPushTaskCore's own return value also changed in this same round: it now returns a CommitAndPushCoreResultV1 discriminated union (`{ kind: "completed" }` / `{ kind: "noChanges" }` / `{ kind: "notCompleted", reason: CommitAndPushNotCompletedReasonV1 }`) instead of a plain "completed"|"noChanges"|"notCompleted" string, so executeCommitPushV1 (commitPushRowV1.ts) can report a specific commitPush.<reason> outcome code (e.g. commitPush.userCancelled, commitPush.pushFailed, commitPush.gitCommitFailed) instead of one undifferentiated commitPush.notCompleted for every non-success stopping point; the Git workflow's own sequencing, prompts, and commands inside commitAndPushTaskCore are otherwise unchanged, so full coordinator-native workflow ownership (as opposed to lease/eligibility/outcome ownership) remains the one still-open gap this route's target row documents in its own header. commitPushMetadata.v1 remains the nested AI sub-step commitPush.v1's execute runs into via reviewCommitMessage; its own route claim moved to a synthetic internal:commitPushMetadata.v1 id (mirroring editExecution.v1) since it is never reached directly from a command.
